To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) UI is not a good solution to the problems created by the market failure in providing unemployment insurance, (ii) UI creates its own problems, and (iii) the alternative to UI, unemployment assistance (UA), is not an ideal solution either, but it is better than UI in most cases.
• The main reason that UI fails is moral hazard.
UI is not an ideal instrument of income support in times of high unemployment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: What is the role of social protection programs in general?
the efficiency of social policy in the face of informational problems, and the role of the state in the provision of insurance against risk of unemployment.
the design and performance of unemployment insurance and unemployment assistance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
unemployment assistance (UA) is not necessarily superior to UI, but that the choice of a particular program depends on the particular circumstances in each case.
UI is an imperfect instrument, but that it is still better than no UI at all, and that its imperfections can be mitigated.
the UI is not an optimal policy instrument to fight unemployment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
UI is a good policy but it is not perfect.
UI is not the only solution to the problem of unemployment and that UI is not a panacea to the problem of poverty.
the EU is in a situation where it is not clear whether it is better off without a UI system, or whether it is better to have a more efficient one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
UI is not the best solution to the problems of unemployment.
UI is an important policy tool, but it is far from perfect and needs to be supplemented and complemented with other policy instruments.
unemployment assistance (UA) is an alternative to UI that is less subject to moral hazard.
